proposal.goal: Factory Next — Live Multi-Target Acceptance Drill: build a small, dependency-free, plain-JavaScript Node.js utility that (1) parses data/readings.csv room/watt readings into structured records with sensible blank-line handling and useful malformed-data errors, with valid/invalid automated tests; (2) provides a deterministic command-line report computing per-room and overall watt totals (sample: kitchen 150, office 75, total 225) with tests; and (3) provides a reusable slugify text utility ("Living Room / North" -> "living-room-north") with tests. Use the built-in Node.js test runner (npm test), introduce no external dependencies, stay inside the current project directory, and do not commit/push/install/deploy or modify Factory source, presets, or existing run artifacts.
constraints: Plain JavaScript only; no TypeScript or transpilation.
No external dependencies of any kind; do not install packages or create node_modules.
Use Node's built-in test runner via the existing `npm test` -> `node --test` script.
Work only inside the current project directory; do not modify anything outside it.
Do not modify Factory source code, production registration, global presets, or the existing .pi/factory run artifacts.
Do not commit, push, install packages, or deploy.
Preserve completed work if a later correction is needed; do not silently omit requirements.
The parser must reject malformed data with useful (not generic) errors.
workPackages: WP1 (readings-parser): implement the reusable CSV readings parser and its valid/invalid node:test suite.
WP2 (slug-utility): implement the reusable slugify text utility and its node:test suite (independent of WP1).
WP3 (cli-report): implement room/overall aggregation, deterministic report formatting, and the CLI entry that consumes the WP1 parser, plus its node:test suite.
acceptanceCriteria: npm test (node --test) completes with zero failures and no external dependencies are installed or declared.
Running the CLI against data/readings.csv deterministically reports kitchen 150 watts, office 75 watts, and 225 watts overall.
The parser has automated valid and invalid input tests, and malformed inputs produce errors with useful line/context information.
The slug utility passes tests including slugify('Living Room / North') === 'living-room-north' and handles capitalization, surrounding whitespace, repeated separators, and punctuation.
The CLI report reuses the parser module rather than re-parsing CSV inline, and its output ordering is deterministic.
No files outside the project directory were modified, and no Factory source, preset, or existing run artifact was changed.
Nothing was committed, pushed, installed, or deployed.
The final report states the actual verified outcome and explicitly accounts for every mission requirement without claiming unverified acceptance.

targets.description: Implement src/readings.js: a reusable, dependency-free parser for the room,watts CSV format. parseReadings(text) returns structured records [{room: string, watts: number}] preserving source order, trimming fields, skipping empty/whitespace-only lines, validating the `room,watts` header, and throwing a descriptive Error (1-based line number + offending content) for malformed rows (bad header, wrong column count, empty room, non-integer watts). readReadingsFile(path) wraps fs to read and parse a file. Add test/readings.test.js covering valid input (including the real data/readings.csv yielding 3 records) and invalid inputs.
acceptanceCriteria: src/readings.js exists, is ESM-importable, and introduces no dependencies.
parseReadings on the contents of data/readings.csv returns exactly [{room:'kitchen',watts:120},{room:'office',watts:75},{room:'kitchen',watts:30}] in source order.
Blank and whitespace-only lines are skipped without error.
Malformed rows throw an Error whose message includes the 1-based line number and offending content, covering: missing/invalid header, missing or extra columns, empty room, and non-integer watts.
test/readings.test.js includes at least one valid case and multiple invalid cases and passes under node --test.

targets.description: Implement src/slug.js exporting slugify(label): trim surrounding whitespace, lowercase, replace runs of non-alphanumeric characters (spaces, punctuation, slashes, repeated separators) with a single hyphen, and strip leading/trailing hyphens. 'Living Room / North' must yield 'living-room-north'. Add test/slug.test.js covering capitalization, surrounding whitespace, repeated separators, and punctuation.
acceptanceCriteria: src/slug.js exists, is ESM-importable, and introduces no dependencies.
slugify('Living Room / North') === 'living-room-north'.
Capitalization is lowercased; surrounding whitespace is trimmed; repeated separators collapse to one hyphen; punctuation is removed/converted.
Output contains only [a-z0-9-] with no leading, trailing, or doubled hyphens for the tested inputs.
test/slug.test.js passes under node --test.

targets.description: Implement src/report.js (pure summarize/format logic) and src/cli.js (command-line entry) that consume the readings-parser module. summarize(readings) computes per-room totals and an overall total with deterministic (sorted) room order; formatReport produces stable text; the CLI reads data/readings.csv by default (optional argv path) and prints the room and overall totals. Sample data must yield kitchen 150, office 75, total 225. Add test/report.test.js covering aggregation values, deterministic formatting/ordering, and the CLI/sample output.
acceptanceCriteria: src/report.js and src/cli.js exist, are ESM-importable/runnable, and introduce no dependencies.
The report-obtaining code paths use the readings-parser module (parseReadings/readReadingsFile) rather than re-implementing CSV parsing inline.
Aggregating data/readings.csv yields kitchen 150, office 75, and overall 225.
CLI output is deterministic: rooms appear in a stable order independent of input row order, and repeated runs produce identical output.
test/report.test.js covers per-room and overall totals, deterministic formatting, and the sample output, and passes under node --test.

humanRequirements: Develop a small, dependency-free Node.js utility that processes room-level electricity readings (plain JavaScript).
Implement a reusable parser for the data/readings.csv format (header followed by room names and integer watt readings) that produces structured records.
The parser must handle blank lines sensibly.
The parser must reject malformed data with useful errors.
Provide automated tests for the parser demonstrating valid and invalid inputs.
Provide a command-line report that uses the parsed readings to calculate total watts per room and the overall total.
Running the report against the sample data must produce 150 watts for kitchen, 75 watts for office, and 225 watts overall.
Keep the CLI report output deterministic and add appropriate automated tests.
Provide a reusable text utility producing URL-friendly slugs from labels.
The slug utility must handle capitalization, surrounding whitespace, repeated separators, and punctuation; 'Living Room / North' must become 'living-room-north'.
Add automated tests for the slug utility.
Use plain JavaScript and the built-in Node.js test runner (node --test).
Do not introduce external dependencies.
Work only inside the current project directory; do not modify anything outside it.
Do not modify Factory's source code, production registration, global presets, or existing Factory run artifacts.
Do not commit, push, install packages, or deploy anything.
Do not run unrelated tests.
Run npm test and perform the necessary focused checks.
Verify the sample data produces the expected room and overall totals.
Ensure the slug utility behaves as specified.

Report the actual terminal outcome and authoritative verdict with: execution targets identified, approved dependencies, each target's implementation and review result, repairs/remediation/blocked targets, files created or modified, actual test results, and whether every requirement was delivered.
Preserve completed work if another part requires correction.
Do not silently omit requirements or report the mission as accepted while required implementation remains unfinished.
If a genuine blocker prevents completion, preserve available work and report the actual partial outcome.

architect.approvedArchitecture: Use the existing ESM, dependency-free Node.js scaffold without changing package.json. Implement independent parser and slug modules under src/, then a report/CLI module that imports the parser. Put focused node:test suites under test/. Preserve source-order records; sort room names for deterministic reporting. The parser contract is the prerequisite for the report; the slug utility has no source dependency on either.
constraints: Work only in this project; do not modify .pi/factory artifacts, Factory source, registration, presets, or files outside the project.
Do not commit, push, install packages, deploy, or run unrelated tests; use plain JavaScript, Node built-ins, and the existing npm test script.

Do not discard completed targets during repairs. After implementation and review, run npm test and focused CLI/sample and slug checks; report actual results and any partial or blocked outcome, then stop.
Do not treat a proposed plan or an unverified implementation as mission acceptance.
correctedWorkPackages: readings-parser: implement the reusable validated CSV parser and parser tests; establish its record/file-reader contract before dependent work.
slug-utility: independently implement slugify and its tests.

cli-report: after readings-parser, implement aggregation, deterministic formatting, CLI integration, and tests. Complete cross-target validation and accurate final reporting after all targets are reviewed.
importantRisks: The human request does not prescribe exact report formatting, negative-watt semantics, or Unicode slug behavior. The packet specifies deterministic formatting and signed safe integer parsing without pretending these are user-imposed formats; test the mandated examples.

Factory's existing .pi/factory run artifacts must not be edited as part of implementation or remediation. Final reporting must reflect the controller's actual target reviews and terminal verdict, not infer success solely from tests.

approvedTargets.description: Create src/readings.js exporting parseReadings(text) and readReadingsFile(path). Parse the room,watts CSV header and subsequent records into source-ordered {room, watts} objects; trim fields and skip whitespace-only lines. Reject malformed input with contextual errors. Create test/readings.test.js.
acceptanceCriteria: The existing data/readings.csv parses to [{room:'kitchen',watts:120},{room:'office',watts:75},{room:'kitchen',watts:30}].

Header is required; validate its two field names, allowing surrounding field whitespace and case-insensitive matching. An absent header, wrong header, empty room, wrong number of columns, empty watts, non-integer watts, or integer outside the safe-number range produces a useful error identifying the 1-based line and offending text (or an EOF marker for an absent header). Signed safe base-10 integers are allowed; do not silently coerce decimal or exponent notation.

Blank/whitespace-only lines are skipped, including around the header; line numbers still refer to physical input lines. Tests demonstrate ordinary and blank-line inputs, actual sample-file reading, and multiple invalid cases.
Module is ESM-importable and uses only Node built-ins; focused parser tests pass.

approvedTargets.description: Create src/slug.js exporting reusable slugify(label) and test/slug.test.js. Normalize capitalization and separators into a URL-friendly lowercase slug without requiring the parser or report.
acceptanceCriteria: slugify('Living Room / North') === 'living-room-north'.

Tests cover capitalization, surrounding whitespace, repeated separators, slashes, and punctuation; tested results have no leading/trailing/doubled hyphens and use only lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens.
Module is ESM-importable, dependency-free, and its focused tests pass.

approvedTargets.description: Create src/report.js with reusable summarize(readings) and formatReport(summary), and src/cli.js with a runnable command-line entry. Use readReadingsFile from src/readings.js, defaulting to the project's data/readings.csv (optionally accepting a file path), then print a deterministic report. Create test/report.test.js. After target reviews, perform mission-wide validation and provide an accurate final report.
acceptanceCriteria: Report code imports and uses the parser's records/file-reader rather than duplicating CSV parsing. Summarization aggregates duplicate rooms and overall watts; room ordering is explicitly sorted and independent of input row order.

Focused tests verify per-room and overall totals, ordering/format stability under reordered input, and the actual CLI output using the sample data; repeated CLI executions produce identical output with kitchen 150 watts, office 75 watts, and overall 225 watts.
CLI is runnable using Node, defaults reliably to the project sample path, and reports file/parse failures usefully with a nonzero exit status. No external dependencies are introduced.

Run npm test and focused sample-CLI and slug checks after all implementation/review/repair work. Record actual test results, files created/modified, each identified target's approved dependencies and implementation/review result, repairs or blockers, actual terminal outcome and authoritative verdict, and whether every mission requirement was delivered; do not claim acceptance for unverified work. Stop after validation and reporting.
